ops.title: F7 is conveyed but never enforced: ClaimHandoff discards the nonce and limits it reads
ops.description:
Confirmed by reading the tree at main 54b76e17.

childside.go:40 ClaimHandoff() returns only handoff.conn. claimSpawnedHandoff() populates
spawnedHandoff{conn, nonce, limits} — readSpawnedHandoff parses DAEMONKIT_SPAWNED_NONCE and
the limits conveyance, validating format only — and then the sole non-test caller drops both
fields on the floor. No public child-side entry adopts the nonce or compares the declared
limits against its own.

wire.RunSpawnedSession (internal/wire/spawned.go:59) is the code that would enforce it. It is
internal and has exactly one caller: its own test at internal/wire/spawned_test.go:38.

childside.go:38 godoc names "ServeSpawned" as the second child-side entry point sharing the
one claim ("A second claim — direct or via ServeSpawned, in either order"). ServeSpawned does
not exist anywhere in the module; that grep returns the godoc line and nothing else. So the
"one claim both child-side entry points share" comment at :48 describes one entry point.

Consequence: the CHANGELOG claim that spawn bounds "cannot skew ... refuses a differing one"
was false for the public surface and has been deleted (Lane B closing pass). What IS real is
per-end enforcement of a declared MaxFrame inside the internal session
(TestSpawnedSessionEnforcesDeclaredMaxFrame, child refuses over-bound at exit 71) — a child
that never runs that session never checks anything.

Found by the Lane B closing refuter; not that lane to fix (childside.go/cmd.go were
DO-NOT-EDIT for the wire-hardening brief). Lane C owns this surface.

ops.text: Either a public entry point adopts nonce+limits and refuses a mismatch, or the conveyance stops being read and the godoc stops claiming it
childside.go:38 no longer names a symbol the module does not define
